title: Food safety surveillance of central kitchens supplying school meals
asked: Mr David Hoe asked what targeted and stepped-up surveillance involves for central kitchens under SFA's risk-based inspection regime, and whether SFA will treat central kitchens supplying school meals as a distinct higher-risk tier with sustained stepped-up surveillance.
response: Ms Goh Hanyan said central kitchens are licensed by SFA and inspected more frequently because of their larger scale, with this applied to caterers serving all consumers including nursing home residents. They are graded under the SAFE framework, and a major food safety lapse leads to downgrading after suspension or court conviction and more regular inspections. Since August 2025, SFA has stepped up checks on central kitchens supplying school meals under MOE's Central Kitchen Meal Model programme. SFA and the Communicable Diseases Agency will continue working with MOE schools and appointed central kitchens to strengthen food safety management from kitchens through transport, storage and distribution.

key_points.point: Central kitchens are licensed by SFA.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: Central kitchens are licensed by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA).

key_points.point: They face more frequent inspections because of their larger scale of food processing or preparation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: They are subjected to more frequent inspections as they have a larger scale of food processing or preparation.

key_points.point: This applies to central kitchens and caterers serving all consumers, including nursing home residents.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: This is consistently applied to central kitchens and caterers serving all consumers, including other vulnerable consumers such as persons in nursing homes.

key_points.point: Central kitchens are graded under the SAFE framework.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: In addition, central kitchens are graded under the Safety Assurance for Food Establishment (SAFE) framework.

key_points.point: A major food safety lapse leads to downgrading after suspension or court conviction and more regular inspections.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: In the event of a major food safety lapse, they will be downgraded upon completion of suspension or Court conviction and inspected more regularly.

key_points.point: Since August 2025, SFA has stepped up checks on central kitchens supplying school meals under MOE's Central Kitchen Meal Model programme.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: Since August 2025, SFA has stepped up checks on central kitchens supplying school meals under the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) Central Kitchen Meal Model programme.

key_points.point: SFA requires importers and manufacturers to comply with food safety requirements, and food establishments should source from licensed importers and manufacturers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: SFA requires all importers and manufacturers to comply with food safety requirements and central kitchens and in fact, all food establishments should source from these licensed importers and manufacturers.

key_points.point: Additional inspections are done if central kitchens have repeated food safety lapses.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: additional inspections are also done on these central kitchens if they are found to have repeated food safety lapses

key_points.point: SAFE Phase 1 was implemented on 19 January 2026.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan

key_points.point: Government procurement takes SAFE grades into account for suppliers and central kitchen providers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: For all Government procurement, we then take into consideration the SAFE grades of these suppliers and central kitchen providers to ensure that they have a proper track record of food safety, due to past inspections and the results of that.

key_points.point: Pre-distribution requirements include a uni-directional process to segregate ready-to-eat from non-ready-to-eat food.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: adopting a uni-directional process, meaning that it helps to segregate ready-to-eat from non-ready-to-eat food products

key_points.point: They must identify critical control points along the food preparation process.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: We also require them to identify what we call critical control points along the food preparation process

key_points.point: They must appoint a food hygiene officer to oversee implementation of these measures.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: we also then require appointment of a food hygiene officer to oversee the implementation of these measures

left_open: Whether SFA will classify central kitchens supplying school meals as a distinct higher-risk tier.
Whether SFA will tighten pre-distribution requirements in light of the recent incident.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered ingredient supplier assurance, extra safeguards for children, operator selection compliance, and pre-distribution checks.
